events.title: Harvard Mark I completed
events.summary: The Harvard Mark I (Automatic Sequence Controlled Calculator) was formally presented at Harvard on August 7, 1944 — a room-sized electromechanical computer built by IBM for the U.S. Navy.
events.about: The Mark I read instructions from punched paper tape and used relays and rotating shafts for arithmetic. Grace Hopper programmed it for naval ballistics — the machine that later inspired her work on compilers and the term "debugging."

narrative.whyChosen: The Mark I was the first large-scale automatic digital computer in the United States.
narrative.whyImportant: It linked university research, IBM manufacturing, and military computation at scale.
narrative.problemSolved: The Navy needed automated solution of differential equations for gunnery and design tables.
